document.abstract: The modern trend toward the use of monopack film presents the photographic technician with the problem of making color separations from the resultant color transparency. These should approach in quality those obtained directly by the use of one-shot cameras. A procedure is outlined to accomplish this, using negative masks to correct for the overlaps in the spectral curves of the dye images in the transparency.
